specialItems.name: Field Trip: Cloudstone Sculpture Park on Whidbey - NE
specialItems.desc:
We'll take the ferry to Whidbey Island to visit Cloudstone Sculpture Park, a hidden gem that features over 500 sculptures by the late sculptor Hank Nelson on a beautiful 20 acre natural landscape. There we'll enjoy a docent-guided 90 minute walking tour and also visit the indoor gallery. Lunch in Langley (paid on own) and take the ferry back. Offered jointly with SE Sector

Note: Sculpture park terrain is short grass and gravel paths, golf cart rides will be available for up to 8 people with limited mobility.

Meadowbrook CC - departure time is at time listed
Magnuson CC - departure time is 20 minutes prior
Northgate Station - departure time is 40 minutes prior

Requests for withdrawal with refund (minus service charge) must be received two weeks before scheduled trip date.

specialItems.name: Tea Ceremony - Chado Urasenke Tankokai Seattle Association
specialItems.desc:
Experience a tranquil 40-minute tea presentation at the Shoseian teahouse in a traditional roji located within the Seattle Japanese Garden.

Tickets: $15, include tea & sweets. Reservations required.

IMPORTANT ATTENDENCE INFORMATION:

Admission - Please note that admission to the garden will need to be purchased separately onsite once you arrive. Tea ceremony tickets DO NOT include admission access to the Japanese Garden. Please allow ample time prior to your tea ceremony to purchase admission tickets.

Parking - Free parking is available in the lot south of the Japanese Garden down to Washington Park. There is additional parking available at the nearby lot by Graham Visitor’s Center in the Arboretum. On weekends, holidays, and days with nice weather the parking lots typically fill up fast. If you are travelling to the garden via car, we recommend allowing yourself adequate time to arrive and find parking well before your scheduled tea ceremony. If possible, try to arrive 45 minutes prior to your ceremony time.

Please note that visitors are encouraged to sit on tatami mats, with bench seating available for those unable to do so. We request participants wear socks or tights (no bare feet), and avoid wearing jeans, rings, and personal fragrances. Guests at tea ceremony are asked to wear masks in the roji garden and Shoseian Teahouse. Our Teahouse is not a restaurant or café and is open only during and for tea ceremonies.


Your hosts - Chado Urasenke Tankokai Seattle Association

Tankokai, the Seattle chapter of Chado Urasenke, is a membership organization for the Urasenke Chado practitioners. Their mission is to promote better understanding and appreciation of the rich culture and spirit of Japan through the art of Chado, "The Way of Tea."

Practiced in Japan for Centuries, the art of the tea ceremony - also called Chado, or The Way of Tea - is imbued with harmony, respect, purity, and tranquility. 16th-century master Sen no Rikyu refined Chado, and the Wabi-Sabi aesthetic of simplicity and humility he taught had widespread influence, including on the architecture of tea gardens.

specialItems.desc: Transportation Only- to the annual Lifelong Recreation Resource Fair.  We'll have 2 hours onsite to intertace with Local Organizations- including nonprofit organizations, healthcare agencies, and local businesses offering personalized resources for aging well in the Seattle area. specialItems.name: Field Trip:  Little Norway
specialItems.desc: Escape to scenic Poulsbo, a charming Scandinavian waterfront town. We will kick off the morning with a crisp ferry ride from Seattle, landing just in time to explore historic Front Street's flat, easy sidewalks. Enjoy your morning browsing local boutiques, visiting maritime galleries, and picking up treats at the iconic Sluys Bakery, followed by a relaxed lunch on your own at your choice of the harborside restaurants or pack a sack lunch to enjoy at the waterfront.

specialItems.desc: Welcome the crisp autumn weather with a classic trip to the beautiful Carpinito Brothers Farm in Kent. Pack a sack lunch to enjoy with the group at the farm's picnic tables, paired with some fresh-pressed apple cider from the market. It is the perfect, relaxed way to enjoy a fall afternoon together. Pack a sack lunch to enjoy with the group at the farm's picnic tables.

Experience a tranquil 40-minute tea presentation at the Shoseian teahouse in a traditional roji located within the Seattle Japanese Garden.

Tickets: $15, include tea & sweets. Reservations required.

IMPORTANT ATTENDENCE INFORMATION:

Admission - Please note that admission to the garden will need to be purchased separately onsite once you arrive. Tea ceremony tickets DO NOT include admission access to the Japanese Garden. Please allow ample time prior to your tea ceremony to purchase admission tickets.

Parking - Free parking is available in the lot south of the Japanese Garden down to Washington Park. There is additional parking available at the nearby lot by Graham Visitor’s Center in the Arboretum. On weekends, holidays, and days with nice weather the parking lots typically fill up fast. If you are travelling to the garden via car, we recommend allowing yourself adequate time to arrive and find parking well before your scheduled tea ceremony. If possible, try to arrive 45 minutes prior to your ceremony time.

Please note that visitors are encouraged to sit on tatami mats, with bench seating available for those unable to do so. We request participants wear socks or tights (no bare feet), and avoid wearing jeans, rings, and personal fragrances. Guests at tea ceremony are asked to wear masks in the roji garden and Shoseian Teahouse. Our Teahouse is not a restaurant or café and is open only during and for tea ceremonies.


Your hosts - Chado Urasenke Tankokai Seattle Association

Tankokai, the Seattle chapter of Chado Urasenke, is a membership organization for the Urasenke Chado practitioners. Their mission is to promote better understanding and appreciation of the rich culture and spirit of Japan through the art of Chado, "The Way of Tea."

Practiced in Japan for Centuries, the art of the tea ceremony - also called Chado, or The Way of Tea - is imbued with harmony, respect, purity, and tranquility. 16th-century master Sen no Rikyu refined Chado, and the Wabi-Sabi aesthetic of simplicity and humility he taught had widespread influence, including on the architecture of tea gardens.

specialItems.name: Family Pumpkin Carving
specialItems.desc: Join us in some Halloween fun! Pumpkin carving and crafts.  $12 per person, $6 each for additional pumpkins. Parent or caregiver must be present during the event. (Pre-registration required.)

specialItems.name: Wonderful Wednesdays (Parents Night)
specialItems.desc: Join us for Wonderful  Wednesdays at Loyal Heights CC. It's the perfect way to give yourself a  mid-week parents night out or take a chance to catch up, talk about what’s  going on and what’s coming up. You can rest easy knowing that your children are  engaged in fun activities such as arts and crafts, group games make new friends  in a safe, trusted place. We will provide a child-friendly dinner and feel free  to bring your children in their evening cozies because, after an evening of fun  with their new friends they will fall fast asleep. Child must be fully Pottey trained. Please notify us of  allergies or food restrictions upon registration.

specialItems.name: Field Trip: Carnation Farms Tour - NE
specialItems.desc:
A repeat offering from this summer due to high interest! Come explore the rich history of Carnation Farms, founded in 1908, and reimagined in 2016 as a non profit with a mission to educate and build a resilient local food system. We'll spend time at an onsite museum and then visit their crops and livestock area. Lunch in Duvall (paid on own) or bring a sack lunch to enjoy outside as you explore the downtown area.

This trip will involve uneven, gravel, and dirt paths at the farm.

Meadowbrook CC - departure time is at time listed
Magnuson CC - departure time is 20 minutes prior
Northgate Station - departure time is 40 minutes prior

Requests for withdrawal with refund (minus service charge) must be received two weeks before scheduled trip date.

specialItems.name: Puppet Show
specialItems.desc:
Ventriloquist Elaine Womack loves to entertain with her puppets: Reggie, the outspoken but less perceptive dog, and Critter, the shy and sensitive cat. Each show brings fun antics and songs that teach a few lessons and laughter to children and adults alike.

Please bring a can food donation for the Ballard Food Bank.

specialItems.name: Teen Outing: Movie Night "Street Fighter"
specialItems.desc:
Get
ready for an action-packed movie outing as we head to the theater to watch the
new Street Fighter! Grab some popcorn, hang out with friends, and watch
legendary characters battle it out, from one of the most iconic video game
franchises of all-time. Candy, popcorn and bottled water will be provided. . Please reach out to Dana Tade at 206-684-4788 if you would like  to ask about a scholarship for this outing.

specialItems.name: Pumpkin Carving
specialItems.desc: Kick off the Halloween season with a family pumpkin carving and decorating night! We'll have pumpkins of all sizes with safe carving tools an paints to create your spooky or funky jack-o-lantern! All ages welcome. *One pumpkin per family. Pumpkin choices are first come, first served. Supplies are limited. Suggested Donation $5

specialItems.name: Magnuson Haunted House
specialItems.desc:
Magnuson Haunted House

Join us for a spooky, spine-tingling walk through the depths of Magnuson Community Center. Listen for the voices of the past (and the future) as you make your way through our dark, winding hallways filled with ghosts and ghouls, but watch where you’re walking – you never know what will be waiting for you around the next corner!

specialItems.name: Montlake Fall Fest
specialItems.desc: Celebrate the season at our Montlake Fall Fest—an evening of fun for the whole family! Purchase a wristband which includes unlimited carnival games, a seasonal craft project, and one ticket each for facepainting and the cupcake walk. Enjoy additional activities like a tot bounce house/toy area, and light refreshments. Costumes are welcome, so come dressed in your autumn best and join the celebration! Recommended for ages 2–12. Register early and pay $8/wristband or $10/wristband at the door! Wristbands needed for child participants, adult chaperones are free!  Be sure to register each child separately.

specialItems.name: Bounce and Swim
specialItems.desc: Green Lake Community Center and Evans Pool are co-hosting a haunted celebration! This event has it all from carnival games and bouncy houses from 6-8 p.m. We'll have one public swim from 7-8pm. It's a family swim where you dodge the floating pumpkins! (Swimsuits and towels are a must!) Canned food donation will be collected at the door to support our local food banks.

specialItems.desc: Contact the Specialized Programs Office for more information. Phone: 206-684-4950, email: PKS_Specialized_Programs@seattle.gov. Participant Information Form must be turned in prior to registration.

specialItems.name: Ballard Soccer Cup - Soccer Tournament
specialItems.desc: Ballard CC’s 2nd ever soccer cup is happening on 10/24! Come play in our 5v5 social soccer tournament from 12pm-4pm. All skill levels are welcome. Sign up individually and request up to two people to have on your team (you will receive an email before the tournament). We’ll put together teams of 6 (5 field players, 1 sub, no goalies) and each team is guaranteed three 20-minute games with the top two teams facing off in a championship game at the end. We’ll be playing on grass, so cleats and shin guards are recommended but not required. Bring a blanket or chairs, come meet new people, and hang out on the field and at the community center. Limited snacks and drinks will be provided. This tournament will be low contact so please come with a good attitude, ready to play and meet new people. Must be 15yrs or older (under 18 please contact Ballard Community Center to register). You’ll receive an email with more information asking about your teammate preferences closer to the tournament date."

dropInItems.desc: Play this fun game using Chinese tiles.  Bring your Mah Jong set if you have one.  Beginners welcome.

dropInItems.name: Drop-In: Family Skate Night
dropInItems.desc: Join us for this popular Bitter Lake family tradition as we put on our skates and get moving! We will have   great music and play fun games. Bring your own skates and blades,   or borrow a pair of ours. Please note: Helmets required and no toy skates allowed.

dropInItems.name: Drop-In: Board Games
dropInItems.desc: Bring your favorite game or try one of ours during some community fun! All ages are welcome, but children under 12 must be accompanied by an adult. Come match with members of your community.

dropInItems.name: Drop-In: Pop-Up Craft Corner
dropInItems.desc: Join us for our Saturday Pop-Up Crafter Corner—a relaxed, drop-in space where families can get creative together. Each session offers a variety of craft supplies/projects for you to explore, experiment with, and combine however you like. Stay for a little while or the whole time—no registration needed. Just drop in and enjoy a fun, creative start to your weekend! Supervision required for kids under age 11.

dropInItems.name: Drop-In: Soul Line Dance
dropInItems.desc: Join this free, fun, and energetic class for all ages. Moving to R&B music will push you through several stages of line dance intensity as we get our heart rates up while inches fall off. This exercise caters to all fitness levels. Brought to you by Seattle Parks and Recreation's Rec4All Grant.

dropInItems.name: Drop-In: Craft Group
dropInItems.desc:
Bring supplies and craft alongside other inspired crafters. From beading to sewing, dyeing, mending, knitting, crocheting, scrapbooking, you name it. If it is portable, bring it in! You can easily find help from others for individual projects. This is not a class, just crafting and discussions. Everyone is welcome.
No need to register instead, please be prepared to scan your free Seattle Parks and Recreation pass and the front desk.

dropInItems.name: Drop-In: Detective Cookie's Chess Club
dropInItems.desc: Children and teens are invited to join this Chess Club. Family and community members are also welcome. Drop by to learn and play chess!

dropInItems.name: Drop-In: Bridge
dropInItems.desc: Drop-in play for bridge players of all skill levels. Not a lesson. No activities 10/12.

dropInItems.name: Drop-In: Self Led Tai Chi
dropInItems.desc: This group practices occur in a relaxed, supportive environment without formal instruction, focusing on mindful movement, balance, and ongoing refinement of the form. The emphasis is on consistency, shared practice, and maintaining the health and meditative benefits of Tai Chi in a friendly group setting.

dropInItems.name: Drop-In: Improv Jam (18+)
dropInItems.desc: All skill levels welcome! Join us for a game-based and guided improv jam. The volunteer lead will adjust the evening activities to participant skill level as the group builds an accessible and supportive space. No experience necessary!

dropInItems.name: Water Polo Adult - Drop In
dropInItems.desc: Learn and play water polo. Beginners are welcome but must know how to swim and tread water. This program is intended for 15+ teens and adults comfortable in deep water.

dropInItems.name: Drop-In: Bridge
dropInItems.desc: Drop in Bridge time, mixed levels.

dropInItems.name: Drop-In: Arts and Crafts
dropInItems.desc: Are you creative and like to paint or design things from scratch? Join our program and find the freedom of expression as we make tie dye t-shirts, bracelets, scented candles, paint, and much more. Must have current E-13.

dropInItems.name: Drop-In: Original Gamers
dropInItems.desc: Join  us monthly for classic games like Scrabble, Dominos, Monopoly, and  Dictionary.  Meet new people, connect, and enjoy community fun. Games are provided, just show up! Meets the 3rd Wednesday of each month. Free.

dropInItems.name: Drop-In: Aroma, a Cooking Class
dropInItems.desc: This easy-to-follow cooking class will teach you basic culinary skill like chopping, slicing, dicing, and sautéing. Take control of your kitchen by learning how to meal plan, shop for food, and help another chef. Food handlers card is required and current E-13.

dropInItems.name: Drop-In: Adult Roller Skating
dropInItems.desc: Lace up, drop in, and roll and glow! Join the fun of  roller skating in a safe and welcoming environment. Whether you’re experienced or new to  skating, we welcome all! Glide in and enjoy the ride. Please bring your own  skates.

dropInItems.name: Drop-In: Henna 101
dropInItems.desc: Learn the basics of Henna! This is a hands-on lesson where you will be handling your own henna tubes while being guided through proper handling techniques.  You will be creating fun designs as well as learning some of the history behind it!

dropInItems.name: Drop-In: Bridge
dropInItems.desc: Drop-in play for bridge players of all skill levels. Not a lesson. No activities 11/27.

dropInItems.name: Drop-In: Youth Tutoring
dropInItems.desc:
Youth Tutoring is an hour-long tutoring session catered to middle school students and led by volunteer high school students and/or the Ballard Recreation Leader.

Need help in school? Drop on in! No registration required.

Want to tutor? Contact: pks_ballardcc@seattle.gov

dropInItems.name: Grown and Gathered (18+): Fork and Film
dropInItems.desc: Back for another food-forward hit! Treat yourself to some movie-themed snacks and enjoy a feel good film: My Big Fat Greek Wedding. No registration required. Only 18+.

dropInItems.name: Grown and Gathered (18+): Creators Circle
dropInItems.desc: Looking to connect with your adult neighbors and do some art? Join us for this season's Creators Circle to break the ice, relax, and enjoy building community.  Bring your favorite project-in-progress or or create using the materials provided. Only 18+.
